title: Traversals
summary: Write the pre-order, in-order and post-order sequences, and explain why in-order is sorted.

hook.goal: Produce the in-order, pre-order and post-order sequences of a BST, and explain why in-order is sorted.

scenario.title: Listing every file
scenario.text: To list every file in a set of nested folders, you have to visit every folder exactly once.
scenario.recall: Does the order you list them in matter?

warmUp.question: In tree T, what is the subtree rooted at 30?

options.reply: Yes: a subtree is a node and everything below it.
A subtree includes everything below the node too.
The subtree includes the node it is rooted at.
50 is above 30, so it is not in 30's subtree.

explore.prompt: When did you write each node down: before, between or after its children?

options.reply: That is pre-order. The other two choices are also traversals; you will see all three next.
That is in-order. The other two choices are also traversals; you will see all three next.
That is post-order. The other two choices are also traversals; you will see all three next.

pages.title: Three ways to walk the tree
steps: A traversal visits every node exactly once.
Pre-order: node, left subtree, right subtree.
In-order: left subtree, node, right subtree.
Post-order: left subtree, right subtree, node.
Memory aid: "pre" is before the children, "in" is between them, "post" is after them.
On the diagram, the dot on the left of a node marks pre-order, below marks in-order, and on the right marks post-order.
pages.caption: Walk around the outside of the tree, starting left of the root. Write a node when you pass the dot for your order.

steps.text: Only in-order is sorted. The BST rule puts every smaller key to the left of a node and every larger key to the right, and in-order writes left, then node, then right.

items.prompt: Why is the in-order sequence of a BST sorted?

options: Every left key is smaller and every right key is larger, so writing left, then node, then right goes from small to large
In-order visits the tree level by level
Insert puts the keys in sorted order
The root is always the middle key

hints.text: In-order writes the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. What does the BST rule say about those?
The in-order dots are shown. Read them from left to right.

items.explanation: The BST rule puts every smaller key on the left and every larger key on the right, and in-order writes left, node, right.
